title: Developing NVIDIA Holoscan Applications with CLI, Skills, and AI Coding Agents | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: NVIDIA's ablation study of AI-coding-agent development on Holoscan/HoloHub found that combining CLI + skills + docs/examples produced the most efficient, highest-quality outcome (40 min, 11M tokens) versus CLI+docs alone (65 min, 20M tokens) or docs alone (40 min, 15M tokens but a 2.6x slower, lower-quality application), with a real endoscopic-segmentation app iteratively optimized to 306.9 FPS (up 50.5%) and 3.247ms mean latency (down 33.6%).

themes.theme: Agentic development workflow for domain-specific SDKs

insights.claim: NVIDIA structured AI-coding-agent development on Holoscan as an iterative engineer-guided loop: the engineer defines a goal and constraints, the coding agent inspects examples and implements code via the CLI, and the engineer reviews code, outputs, and tests before setting the next goal -- explicitly decomposing objectives into small, verifiable iterations rather than a single large prompt.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: A reusable engineering-management pattern for deploying coding agents on complex domain SDKs: decompose by uncertainty/evidence rather than attempting end-to-end generation in one shot.
insights.locator: Instead of trying to build the entire application with a single prompt

insights.claim: The workflow used Codex with GPT-5.6 Sol at max reasoning effort as the coding agent, and NVIDIA describes the workflow itself as agent-agnostic, with the Holoscan CLI (via ./holohub wrapper) providing the shared execution interface for both the agent and the engineer.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: Confirms NVIDIA is building agent-agnostic tooling (CLI + skills) rather than betting on one specific coding-agent vendor, reducing platform-lock-in risk for its developer-tooling strategy.

themes.theme: Iterative build: endoscopic tool segmentation app

insights.claim: In Iteration 1, the coding agent built a working endoscopic tool segmentation application from a single prompt in 40 minutes, connecting video replay, preprocessing, TensorRT inference, SDK segmentation postprocessing, telemetry, and HoloViz visualization, reusing the existing MONAI endoscopic tool segmentation model and sample video without modifying model weights.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: Demonstrates a concrete, timed baseline (40 min) for agent-built medical-imaging edge applications on Holoscan, useful for estimating developer-productivity gains in regulated healthcare-device software workflows.
insights.locator: The agentic processing time was 40 minutes

insights.claim: In Iteration 3, after the agent confirmed inference still ran on every frame and declined to cache/reuse masks across neighboring frames (deferring that policy decision), lower-risk optimizations (reusing HoloViz input specs/static tensors, asynchronous double-buffered telemetry copy) raised rendered throughput from 204.0 FPS to 306.9 FPS (+50.5%), cut mean application-path latency from 4.891ms to 3.247ms (-33.6%), and cut P95 latency from 6.273ms to 4.554ms (-27.4%), consistently across all five measured trials.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: A concrete, reproducible performance-optimization case study (>50% throughput gain, ~34% latency reduction) achieved by an AI coding agent on a real-time medical-imaging pipeline without touching the underlying inference model -- evidence of tangible agentic-engineering ROI.
insights.locator: The optimized version was faster in all five measured trials

themes.theme: Ablation study: CLI + skills + docs vs. partial tooling

insights.claim: In a controlled ablation (same coding agent, sandbox, and prompt; Codex 0.146.0 with GPT-5.6 Sol at max reasoning effort, snapshot Aug. 1), providing the coding agent CLI + skills + docs/examples produced the most efficient outcome: 40 minutes and 11M tokens to a complete, correctly-structured application using standard Holoscan operators.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: Quantifies the token/time cost of the best-resourced agent configuration, a baseline for evaluating NVIDIA's 'skills' investment ROI against raw documentation access.

insights.claim: Removing HoloHub development skills but keeping CLI guidance and docs/examples increased agentic processing time to 65 minutes and token cost to 20M (versus 40 min/11M with skills) -- the agent still built a complete, working application but used generic Bash tools requiring more trial-and-error, such as applying generic linting tools before CLI-based linting or attempting to install Python dependencies directly on the host instead of in the container.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: Isolates the specific value of 'skills' (packaged, project-specific sequences/checks) versus raw CLI+docs access: roughly 1.6x more tokens and 1.6x more time without them -- a measurable ROI case for investing in agent-skill packaging over documentation alone.

insights.claim: With only docs/examples (no CLI guidance, no skills), the agent still inferred and used the CLI from codebase examples, taking 40 minutes and 15M tokens, but produced materially worse code quality: incorrectly embedded third-party model config, an unnecessary Dockerfile that ignored the existing HoloHub base image, and a version that ran 2.6x slower than the other two configurations because it bypassed existing optimized Holoscan operators (TensorRT inference, format converter) in favor of custom PyTorch/MONAI inference.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: Shows that documentation/examples alone can produce a similarly fast but functionally worse (2.6x slower) result than structured CLI+skills guidance -- a caution against assuming 'agent read the docs' is sufficient for production-quality output in specialized domains.
insights.locator: this version is 2.6x slower then the other two settings

insights.claim: Across the three ablation configurations, the combination of CLI, skills, and documentation/examples provided the best developer experience with the lowest resource overhead, indicating that skill design and tooling completeness materially affect coding-agent efficiency and code quality on domain-specific SDKs, not just prompt quality or model choice.
insights.speaker: Wenqi Li
insights.so_what: Supports an investment thesis that 'agent skill packaging' is becoming a distinct, monetizable layer of developer infrastructure alongside SDKs and documentation, relevant to how platform vendors like NVIDIA should allocate developer-relations resources.
insights.quote: the combination of CLI, skills, and documentation/examples provided the best developer experience with the lowest resource overhead
insights.locator: While follow-up prompts could potentially address these issues
